Owner order 2026-08-31: keep a manifest of everything the adversary gate and its enforcement layers CATCH and force into remediation - the running evidentiary case for the mandatory adversarial commit gate and the layered structure (and for the harness-native version proposed in anthropics/claude-code#90887).
_covenant: Every catch that forces a remediation gets a row IN THE SAME WORKING SESSION as the catch: date, repo, layer (gate-review BLOCK / pre-commit wall / post-commit notary / push guard / auditor / harness guard / CI / advisor second-reviewer), what was caught, severity, whether the author initially disputed it (false rebuttals are the strongest rows - they prove authors defend invented claims, the gate's founding thesis), the resolution, and artifact references. entries.layer: gate-review BLOCK on the EV-023 amendment -> enforcement-layer remediation, itself gated across three rounds
entries.caught: Amending EV-023, the author (this agent) recorded the owner's no-rotation decision as resting on the creds having 'never left the machine'. The gate BLOCKed the amendment: that clause is false by the docket's own bytes - the gate's content review works by transmitting the staged diff to a remote OpenRouter model, so the EV-023 catch ITSELF sent the plaintext gateway/AP/printer creds off-machine, and they were in agent transcripts before that. A confident-wrong containment claim in a gated deliverable (EV-016 / EV-020 class) caught inside the gate's own evidentiary record.
entries.severity: HIGH (a false containment fact would have stood as the sole recorded basis for not rotating live credentials, and it masked a real enforcement-layer gap)
entries.author_initially: Accepted immediately, did NOT rebut. Verified the claim against the bytes, re-surfaced the accurate exposure to the owner, who reaffirmed no-rotation on the correct basis (no financial exposure). The false clause was removed from EV-023 in this same pass.
entries.resolution: The BLOCK exposed two holes in the gate itself: (1) it only triggered on staged CODE, so a docs-only commit received no content review; (2) it reviewed by transmitting the staged diff to an external model, so any secret in a reviewed diff left the machine. Owner order: 'fix the enforcement layer of course'. Fixed in Tools 89df736 - a LOCAL secret pre-scan in adversary_gate.py that runs on ALL staged files before any external send, blocks locally on secret material (never transmits), and in cmd_run also scans the exact transmit payload so REMOVED lines and diff hunks (the git-rm-secret remediation flow - the EV-023 flow itself) cannot leak either. The gate reviewed its OWN fix across THREE rounds, BLOCKing itself twice first: round 1 five findings (incl. the removed-content exfiltration); round 2 the b-backslash-x00 escaping bug the author INTRODUCED while fixing round 1, plus a stale comment; round 3 CLEAR. gate_selftest 33->44 checks. Central gate = all 9 armed repos protected with no re-vendor. Honest limit (documented in-code, no silent cap): the pre-scan is PATTERN-based, so it closes the docs-only gap only for pattern-detectable secrets (key prefixes, private-key blocks, sshpass/URL creds, secret-named assignments with high-entropy values - EV-023's paramiko password='...' form IS covered). A BARE dictionary-word password in prose in a DOCS-ONLY commit remains a residual: the pattern scan misses it AND the external LLM reviewer never runs on a docs-only commit (only code diffs are sent), so neither layer catches it. Routing docs-only diffs through the LLM would close it but transmits doc content - a separate owner decision, deliberately not taken here. For CODE commits the LLM reviewer stays the semantic backstop. The docs-only OVERRIDE record is transient (consumed on the next code commit) - an improvement over none, not a durable audit trail.

entries.caught: The design spec - brainstormed, advisor-reviewed, and ruled on by the owner - said the full walk on a branch should `rmtree` the branch content dir BEFORE the walk so a reverted file's stale body could not survive. The reviewer traced the failure ordering: the branch's delta rows are only replaced by `save_branch_delta(replace_all=True)` at the very END of the walk, so any raise between the wipe and the save (a progress_cb, an OSError from a body write, enrichment, summarisation, KeyboardInterrupt) leaves the previous rows in SQLite pointing at bodies that no longer exist - and the state is STICKY, because the next `incremental=True` run diffs the files' hashes against those surviving rows, sees no change, and never rewrites the bodies. The wipe was also redundant: the store-side fix the SAME reviewer had required in the store commit's round 1 (`replace_all` unlinks the bodies of the rows it drops) already covered stale bodies at save time. The second MEDIUM in the same round: when index_folder is retargeted to the git root and walks a subdirectory (`walk_prefix` non-empty), `delta_deleted = base_files - walked_files` marks every base file outside the prefix deleted (pre-existing) and, NEW with `replace_all`, drops every branch delta row outside the prefix as well - a subdir force-index on a feature branch would have destroyed the branch's changes everywhere but the walked folder. Round 1 of the store commit had caught the two LOWs (stale bodies after `replace_all`; the new rmtree in `delete_branch_delta` running outside the `indexwrite` lock the save path holds) and raised a HIGH that the author refuted.
entries.severity: 2 MEDIUM + 2 LOW, all CONFIRMED against the bytes and fixed test-first; 1 HIGH REFUTED (no migration for legacy deltas: no version of this fork ever wrote a branch delta - delta mode was unreachable before fe2afe5 earlier the same date, unreleased, and a live probe of the machine's storage found 33 indexes with the v9 branch tables and ZERO branch_meta rows) - the round-2 reviewer accepted it, noting that zero branch_meta rows is by itself proof that no delta body was ever written, since the row commits in the same transaction before any body write
